title: Tenali and the Tax Collector

full_text:
In the eastern district of Vijayanagara served a ruthless royal tax collector named Bhupati, who levied unauthorized extra taxes upon poor potters, washermen, and blacksmiths, claiming it was the 'Emperor’s Weight Assessment'. When the poor pleaded that they had no money, Bhupati confiscated their tools and beasts of burden.

A delegation of weeping artisans arrived at Tenali Raman’s door, begging for intervention.
Tenali comforted them: 'Go back to your workshops, brothers. Tomorrow, Bhupati shall feel the true weight of his assessment.'

The next morning, while King Krishnadevaraya was holding court, a tremendous commotion arose outside the palace gates.
Tenali Raman entered the audience hall, puffing and groaning, carrying upon his shoulders an enormous, healthy grey donkey!
The donkey was kicking its legs and braying loudly:
*‘HEE-HAW! HEE-HAW!’*

The King and the entire court stared in disbelief.
The King cried: 'Tenali! Have you lost your senses? Why are you carrying a kicking donkey on your shoulders into the royal diwan?'

Tenali carefully set the donkey down upon the marble floor, bowed, and gasped for breath:
'Jahanpanah! I am merely obeying the latest revenue regulation established by your district collector, Master Bhupati!'

Bhupati, who was present in the court, turned pale.
The King demanded: 'What regulation?'
Tenali explained:
'Collector Bhupati has decreed that every citizen must pay taxes based on the weight of their heaviest working possession.
A poor washerman owns only this donkey to carry laundry. Since Bhupati threatened to confiscate the beast unless the washerman carried it to the palace to be officially weighed, I offered to carry it for the poor man!
Now, Maharaj, order the imperial scales brought forth, so we may weigh this donkey and calculate how much silver this poor beast owes to the crown!'

The court erupted in roaring laughter.
King Krishnadevaraya turned his blazing gaze upon the trembling collector:
'Bhupati! Is this how you represent my name among the people? By forcing working men to carry impossible burdens?'

An immediate audit of Bhupati’s district books revealed massive embezzlement.
The King dismissed Bhupati, confiscated his ill-gotten wealth to compensate the cheated artisans, and abolished all unlawful assessments.
Tenali was rewarded by the artisan guilds with woven silk and brass lamps, proving that courageous humor can lift the heaviest yokes of oppression.
moral: Public servants who burden the poor with unlawful extortions deserve to carry the weight of their own greed.
